result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.ego_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Extract the neighborhood around a node as a new graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.ego_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Extract the neighborhood around a node as a new graph. title: >- [Graph.ego_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Extract the neighborhood around a node as a new graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Extract the neighborhood around a node as a new graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L42614-L42758){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.ego_graph( node, radius=1, center=True, mode="out", weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Ego graph](../assets/graphs/ego-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A six-node graph with node ids in pills; the ego C is outlined. Its radius-1 ego graph keeps C, its neighbors B, D, and E, and every edge among them, including B-D, which does not touch C, all in the accent color; A and F are dropped and shown dashed. The new graph keeps the labels but renumbers the ids 1 to 4." width="100%"} The ego graph (or ego network) of a node is the subgraph induced by the node and every node within `radius=` of it: its neighbors at radius 1, their neighbors too at radius 2, and so on, along with all edges among them. Ego networks are the standard unit of personal-network analysis in sociology ("who are this person's contacts, and how do they know each other?"), and a convenient way to zoom in on one part of a large graph. Distance follows the same rule as `shortest_path()`: hops on an unweighted graph, total edge weight on a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`), unless `weighted=` says otherwise. Note that with weights, `radius=` is a weight budget, not a hop count. Labels, node attributes and edge attributes are kept in the new graph and, as with `subgraph()`, nodes and edges keep their IDs. This is a one-call version of `select_nodes_in_neighborhood()` followed by `transform_to_subgraph_ws()`, and leaves the current selection alone. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The center (the "ego"), as an integer ID or a string label. [radius]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Include nodes at distance at most this from the center. Default is `1`. [center]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), include the center node itself; if `False`, return only its surroundings. [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which way to measure distance on a directed graph: `"out"` follows edges from the center (default), `"in"` follows them backward (who can reach the center), and `"all"` ignores direction. Ignored for undirected graphs. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to measure distance by edge weight. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph containing the ego network. The original graph is not modified. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the node does not exist, `mode=` is invalid, `radius=` is negative, or weights are used and one is negative. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The radius-1 ego network of C holds C, its three neighbors, and the edges among them, including B-D, which does not touch C: ::: {#9a0bf6cd .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "E"), ("E", "F")]) ) ego = graph.ego_graph("C") sorted(ego.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['B--C', 'B--D', 'C--D', 'C--E'] ``` ::: ::: A larger radius reaches further out, and `center=False` leaves the ego out: ::: {#7d5a7411 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} wider = graph.ego_graph("C", radius=2) around = graph.ego_graph("C", center=False) sorted(wider.get_node_df()["label"]), sorted(around.get_node_df()["label"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F'], ['B', 'D', 'E']) ``` ::: ::: On a directed graph, `mode=` decides between followers and followees: ::: {#e5fd0972 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} follows = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["me", "a", "b", "c"]) .add_edges([("me", "a"), ("me", "b"), ("c", "me")]) ) ( sorted(follows.ego_graph("me", mode="out").get_node_df()["label"]), sorted(follows.ego_graph("me", mode="in").get_node_df()["label"]), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (['a', 'b', 'me'], ['c', 'me']) ``` ::: :::
